quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to finish the pass.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete all passes at legal speeds. Pass only where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them easier to see.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Hold the clutch and brakes ready to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach an intersection. Choose a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers. Get your clutch and brakes ready to react quickly. Do not change your speed or position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: Before riding, check your clutch. A working clutch should feel:
questions.correctAnswerText: Tight and smooth.
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when released. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is easiest to see when riding in which lane position?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best when following a car. It places you in the driver's rearview mirror where they can see you. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions require it.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle, position yourself:

options.text: To be seen in the vehicle's side mirror.
To be seen in the vehicle's rearview mirror.
To be seen through the vehicle's passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: To be seen in the vehicle's rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of your lane behind the car. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: A gravel road
questions.explanation: Poor traction surfaces include wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and steel plates or utility hole covers.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
Check your mirrors only. Look over your shoulder only if something seems unusual.
Either check your mirrors or look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Make sure no other vehicles are in your path.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:
questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the operator and hold firmly to the operator's waist or hips. They can also hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
Can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to increase how easily other drivers can see you, even during the day. Clothes with reflective materials are also helpful.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cause you to lose control.
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes can cause you to lose control. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again right away. If your rear brake locks while stopping on a surface with good grip, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the road ahead.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be used during the day.
Be used without a driver license.
Be used with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: You are most likely to have a collision:
questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection.
questions.explanation: The most dangerous place for a collision is at an intersection, where you and other traffic are most likely to meet.

questions.question: The best way to avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle ride is to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent breaks to rest.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long ride, limit your riding time each day and take frequent rest breaks. Do not use stimulants because you will feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while you are stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually stay in control.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually stay in control.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle will usually stay under control if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: White signs with red and black markings are regulatory signs. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to dangers.
You will have room to move.
You will have more time to speed up when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to speed up when turning.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react quickly and move out of the way if another driver makes a mistake. It does not give you more time to speed up in curves.

questions.question: A sign that your rear tire is suddenly flat is:

options.text: The back of your motorcycle is moving from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle is moving from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire goes flat, the back of your motorcycle may jerk or sway from side to side. If you feel this movement, stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Which brake is stronger on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It can stop about 70 percent of the motorcycle by itself.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle passenger do?

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle stops.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Ride at the same speed as you would during the day.
Ride slower than you would during the day.
Ride faster than you would during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night, especially on unfamiliar roads. Slower speed gives you more time to see and avoid hazards when visibility is poor.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it:
questions.correctAnswerText: Has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and be free of cracks, loose padding, and frayed straps.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road shows:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in their blind spot. The driver will not see you. Also, the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears.
